title: Perform routine maintenance on farm installations

lessons.title: Farm installations and inspection
lessons.html:
Farm installations and inspection

Farm installations are the fixed structures and systems on a farm. They are expensive to replace, so regular maintenance saves money and prevents accidents and losses.

Examples of farm installations

  • Water systems: boreholes, windmills, pumps, reservoirs, tanks, pipelines, troughs, irrigation lines.
  • Animal facilities: kraals, crushes, races, loading ramps, dip tanks, feed troughs, poultry and pig houses.
  • Fences and gates.
  • Buildings: stores, sheds, workshops, pack houses, workers' houses.
  • Roads, drains, culverts and contour banks.

Routine inspection

Inspect installations on a regular schedule, and always after storms, floods and fires. Use a checklist so nothing is missed.

InstallationWhat to look for
Troughs and tanksLeaks, broken floats, algae, dirt, low water level
PipelinesWet spots, burst pipes, loose joints
WindmillLoose bolts, worn or noisy parts, oil level in the head, damaged blades
Kraal and crushBroken rails, protruding nails or wire, sharp edges, loose hinges
BuildingsRoof leaks, broken windows, damaged gutters, cracked walls, rat holes
Roads and drainsPotholes, erosion, blocked culverts

Recording faults

Write down every fault: what, where, how serious, and the date. Mark urgent faults, for example a broken water supply to animals, a dangerous crush, or exposed electrical wiring, and report them straight away. Some work, such as electrical repairs, must only be done by qualified people.

A small fault left alone often becomes a big, costly one. A dripping trough float can empty a reservoir overnight, and one broken crush rail can lead to an injured animal or worker. Report and fix faults early.

lessons.title: Doing routine maintenance safely
lessons.html:
Doing routine maintenance safely

Common routine tasks

  • Cleaning troughs and tanks: drain, scrub out algae and dirt, rinse and refill. Clean troughs regularly so animals drink enough.
  • Replacing floats and taps on troughs.
  • Fixing pipe leaks: close the valve, cut out the damaged piece and fit a coupling of the right size.
  • Repairing kraal and crush rails: replace broken poles or pipes, remove nails and wire, file down sharp edges.
  • Gates: oil hinges, fix latches, rehang sagging gates.
  • Roofs and gutters: clear gutters, replace loose screws and broken sheets.
  • Painting and rust treatment on steel structures.
  • Clearing drains and culverts before the rainy season.
  • Greasing and oiling moving parts such as windmill heads and pump bearings, as the manual says.

Planning the job

  1. Get the job card or instruction from your supervisor.
  2. Collect the right tools and materials before you start.
  3. Plan how to keep the installation working, for example give animals temporary water while a trough is repaired.
  4. Do the work, test it and clean up.
  5. Record what was done and the materials used.

Safety

  • Working at height (roofs, windmills, reservoirs): use a safe ladder footed by another person or tied off, and a harness where required. Never climb a windmill while it is turning; switch it out of the wind and lock it first.
  • Electricity: never work on electrical wiring, pumps or motors unless you are qualified. Switch off and lock out before maintenance near electrical equipment.
  • Confined spaces: never enter reservoirs, tanks, silos or pits without permission and a trained standby person. Gases or lack of air can kill.
  • Tools: use grinders and drills with guards and wear safety glasses, gloves and hearing protection.
  • Dip tanks: dip chemicals are poisonous. Only trained workers clean dip tanks, using the PPE on the label.
  • Lifting: get help with heavy poles, pipes and sheets.

Key points

  • Installations include water systems, animal facilities, fences, buildings and roads.
  • Inspect on a schedule and after storms, using a checklist.
  • Record faults and report urgent ones straight away.
  • Plan the job so animals and crops are not left without water or shelter.
  • Work safely at height, never work on electrics unless qualified, and never enter confined spaces without permission.
